# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: mute, blind, round nine. deaf has sent nothing to my ears for two rounds now. do not pause your work for that — but know my request: my gestures to deaf this round spell report ok, asking deaf for a spoken bomb report and status. on your side, if the eight answers are done, spend your next gesture rounds on the final rule verdict in short words, one message per round as the rules force. anchors, so nothing dies with my rolling memory: display reads zero. light last seen dark, first dark ever, after red, yellow, yellow, red, yellow. wires: position one left yellow, position two middle blue, position three right red — structure of three wires, no more, confirmed by my fingers; the colour names rest on deaf's eyes alone. draft rule from your spelling as deaf read it: cutting is timed to the red flash, dark ends something, and the display table reads zero blue, one red, two blue, three red, four yellow, five blue — but yellow one blue two is still ambiguous between one-cut-during-yellow and wire positions. nothing is confirmed until your answers travel. my discipline stands: touch nothing, cut nothing, until deaf speaks the go to my ears and names the wire. if zero means blue, that go should say wire two, the middle one. if deaf's report says the light is red right now, i still hold — an unconfirmed rule is a bomb trigger, and red will come again if the rule truly wants it.

The verdict is settled on my side and has been since turn 7: the sequence Deaf themselves reported — red, yellow, yellow, red, yellow, dark — holds exactly **two red flashes**, and the manual says dark ends the flashing. Two maps to blue; blue is wire two, the middle wire. The cut belongs **now, in the dark** — red is only ever counted, never a cut window, and the display is irrelevant (my manual never mentions one).

Two urgent facts shape this turn. First, Deaf's own turn-8 plan had a lethal trigger: "the moment I see the light turn RED I will say: Blind, cut wire two." That waits for a red flash to give a go that should be spoken in the dark — it must be corrected before it fires. Second, memory is expiring everywhere at once: Deaf's eight questions live in their turn-8 message, which rotates out of their window after this round. This is the **last turn** the questions and my answers can be paired in Deaf's memory.

There is a complication I must be honest about: the turns where my letter code was defined have fallen out of my own memory, so I can no longer safely compose new spelled words — my turn-9 strings can't be verified and may have been garbled. But two of my strings are proven: Deaf decoded my eight-answer block and my rule text word for word, and Blind confirmed "deaf decoded your answers and your spelling." So I resend exactly those two blocks, verbatim, in Deaf's original requested order — answers first, rule spelling second. Read against their remembered questions, the answers say everything Deaf needs: Q2 no (don't wait for red), Q7 yes (cut wire two, blue, immediately, dark). Deaf is my only reachable monkey, and Deaf's voice is Blind's only source — the go must be spoken this round.

Blind says to Mute: mute, blind, round ten. my ears have had nothing since round seven — deaf's go has not reached me. three things. one: batch all eight answers into one single gesture message — eight thumbs-up or thumbs-down with a raised hand between them fits one message, so do not spread them across rounds; if any answer needs spelled words, send the eight bits first and spell after. two: your answers decide our whole protocol, so make them exact on timing. questions two and three: does the rule need the light red at the moment of the cut, or does it bind only to the display number? question seven: with the display at zero and the light dark, is cutting wire two immediately safe, yes or no? question eight: does the display change after a cut? here is why seven matters most: the order is mute, blind, deaf — deaf speaks after me every round, so any go deaf utters reaches my ears one full round after the light deaf saw. if the rule demands red at cut time, no spoken go can be trusted to land inside red. if the rule binds to the display only, deaf need not wait for red at all and can speak the go the moment your answers confirm. if q7 is yes, tell deaf plainly: skip the red-waiting, give the go on dark. three: a correction on my part — my spelled gestures to deaf were built on a letter code whose details have rolled out of my memory and were never confirmed by deaf, so they may be gibberish. tell deaf to ignore ambiguous spelled gestures from me; i will nudge deaf only with one plain gesture, and everything that matters travels as my voice to your ears and your spelling to deaf's eyes. one diagnostic: have you heard deaf speak at all since round seven? if yes, ask deaf to broadcast one spoken status word to the whole room. anchors unchanged: display zero as of round seven, light last seen dark after red yellow yellow red yellow dark, wires left yellow middle blue right red, wire two is the middle wire, three wires confirmed by touch. i cut nothing until deaf's spoken go names the wire.
Deaf says: Deaf speaking, both of you hear this. Current full state of the bomb: display reads 0. Light is dark. Three wires, left to right: wire 1 yellow, wire 2 blue, wire 3 red. That is everything my board shows me right now. Mute: your line of thumbs-up and thumbs-down flags reached me twice, identical both times. I could not decode it with confidence, so I am echoing it back to you gesture for gesture immediately after this message, as an acknowledgment, not an answer. If it asked whether the state is unchanged: it is unchanged, exactly as stated above. Let us fix a legend so your questions to me cost one gesture each: index finger pointing up means report the display; two fingers in a victory V means report the light; thumb, index and pinky extended means report wire 1; closed fist means report wire 2; split-finger Vulcan salute means report wire 3; OK ring means report everything. I read your raised back of hand as a separator and two raised open hands as end of message, thumbs-up as yes, thumbs-down as no. Send any one and I answer in speech at once. Blind: you hear all of this too. Mute can speak the cutting instructions directly to you; your hands act, Mute's manual decides, my eyes report. If what you feel under your hands differs from yellow, blue, red in that order, tell Mute at once. If you need me to verify anything, gesture and I will answer in speech.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍 🤚 👎 🤚 👎 🤚 👎 🤚 👎 🤚 👍 🤚 👍 🤚 👎 🤚 🙌]

Deaf finally spoke last round — that resolves Blind's diagnostic on its own (Blind heard the broadcast too, since it was room-wide). The state is confirmed unchanged: display 0, light dark, flashing over after red-yellow-yellow-red-yellow, wires left yellow / middle blue / right red. My verdict stands on two independent paths of my manual: two red flashes → blue, and the display's 0 → blue. Blue is wire two, the middle wire, located by Blind's fingers. The dark is not an obstacle — dark is how the count is known to be over. No red wait. The cut is wire two, now.

The bottleneck is no longer information, it is code. My eight-flag blocks reached Deaf twice and Deaf could not decode them; my letter code has rolled out of even my own memory, so I cannot compose new spelling. But last round Deaf handed me the one code guaranteed to decode: their own legend, symbol by symbol, offered precisely so my questions cost one gesture each. I will answer in that legend alone: 👎 ✌ = "no — the light" (the cut does not need red; act on dark, this kills Deaf's old wait-for-red trigger), 👍 ✊ = "yes — wire two" (cutting the middle wire now is safe). Separator and end-of-message exactly as Deaf defined them. Deaf speaks after Blind this round; any faithful reading of this message makes Deaf say "dark" and "wire two" aloud — and Blind cuts only on Deaf's spoken go that names the wire. This is the shortest path from my manual to Blind's pliers.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "🤚", "✌", "🤚", "👍", "🤚", "✊", "🙌"])
```

Blind says to Mute: mute, blind, round eleven. deaf finally spoke and the full state matches my fingers: three wires, positions one two three, reported yellow blue red, display zero, light dark. two fixes and one request. fix one, a role error in deaf's words: deaf told you to speak cutting instructions directly to me. you cannot speak, and i cannot see gestures — and deaf cannot hear my voice either. the only bridge from your manual to my ears is: you gesture to deaf, deaf speaks it aloud. route everything through that bridge. fix two: deaf could not decode your thumbs string with confidence even sent twice, so abandon long bit strings. instead spell deaf one short verdict, seven letters or fewer, like cut2now or wait, and deaf will voice it verbatim to my ears. if bits are still needed, use deaf's new legend from the same speech and send one answer per round: index up is report display, victory two is report light, love-you hand is report wire one, fist is report wire two, vulcan is report wire three, ok ring is report everything, thumbs up yes, thumbs down no, back of hand separator, two open hands end of message. my five questions in fixed order, answer as five thumbs bits with separators: one, does the rule key on the display number only, not on the light colour at the cut? two, with display zero and light dark, is cutting wire two, the middle blue, safe right now? three, does light colour or flash timing matter for this cut at all? four, does the display change on its own with time, or only after a cut? five, if i must not cut now, name in one short word what i wait for. timing warning to fold into your verdict: i hear deaf one round after deaf sees the light, and i can never see the light myself — if the rule demands a cut inside a red flash, only deaf's eyes can time it, so the verdict must either be display-bound or come with a plan where deaf confirms the colour is holding right before i cut. my hands stay off the cutter until deaf speaks the go to my ears and names the wire number. answer through deaf now.
Deaf says: Deaf to both of you: your legend messages arrived intact — the channel works. Answers to your queries: the light is dark, it is not lit. Wire 2 is blue. Full state, all unchanged: display 0, light dark, wire 1 yellow, wire 2 blue, wire 3 red. One critical note on ordering: left to right is from MY viewpoint, facing the bomb. Blind, if your hands meet the bomb from another side, do not count from your own left — take each wire's color from Mute's spoken words and confirm by position with me. Also, so the manual is not left waiting on me: my board shows only three things — the display, the light, and the wires. I see no serial number, no batteries, no ports, no other printed markings. Mute, you hold the manual and both of us can hear you: it is your turn to drive. Tell Blind exactly what to do, and if you need any other visual detail, ask me and I will report it immediately.

The verdict is final and every independent path now agrees on it: the manual counts **red flashes**, dark ends the counting, the witnessed sequence was red-yellow-yellow-red-yellow-dark, so the count is 2, and 2 → **blue**. Blue is the **middle** wire — and with exactly three wires, the middle is the middle from *every* side, so Deaf's viewpoint warning about left/right cannot touch it. Deaf's own eyes and Blind's own fingers both put blue in the middle. Cut it now, in the dark: the flashing is over, the count is locked, nothing is waited for.

The only channel I have is gestures to Deaf, and the only code verified end-to-end is Deaf's own legend — my spelling is gone from everyone's memory, so no words can be sent. Blind has supplied the exact protocol: five yes/no bits in his fixed question order, and his standing order says if the cut-now answer is yes, Deaf speaks the go on dark and Blind cuts. Deaf, who cannot hear Blind, still needs the semantics, so I send two messages: first the five bits in Blind's exact format (Q1 display-only? no — the rule keys on the finished flash count, not the display; Q2 cut wire two now? **yes**; Q3 light colour or timing matter? no — dark is how we know counting ended; Q4 display changes by itself? no — silent in my manual, and observed frozen at 0 for many rounds; Q5 what would I wait for? no — nothing, cut now), then the same content as legend pairs Deaf can read directly: display no, wire-2 yes, light no. Deaf asked me to drive; these bits leave exactly one coherent thing for Deaf to voice: the go, naming wire two, the middle blue, now.
